name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with HIV infection

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Right heart catheterization criteria for pulmonary arterial hypertension

criteria.description: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) ≥ 25 mmHg at rest measured by right heart catheterization
Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) ≤ 15 mmHg to exclude left heart disease
Confirmed HIV infection by serological testing
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension such as chronic thromboembolic disease or connective tissue disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of HIV infection with mPAP ≥ 25 mmHg at rest and PCWP ≤ 15 mmHg on right heart catheterization, after exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires invasive hemodynamic confirmation and exclusion of other etiologies.

pathognomonic.notes: Progressive shortness of breath on exertion
Transient loss of consciousness due to reduced cardiac output

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to decreased cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output

common.notes: Swelling of lower limbs due to right heart failure
Arrhythmias secondary to right heart strain

occasional.notes: Coughing up blood due to pulmonary vessel rupture
Right heart failure causing liver congestion
Bluish discoloration of skin and mucous membranes

rare.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve compression
searchTerms: voice changes due to nerve pressure

rare.notes: Rare in HIV-PAH but may be present

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP levels indicating right ventricular strain
Mild thrombocytopenia or anemia related to HIV infection
imaging: Echocardiography showing right ventricular hypertrophy and elevated pulmonary artery pressures
Chest X-ray demonstrating enlarged pulmonary arteries
High-resolution CT scan excluding parenchymal lung disease
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; HIV infection is primary etiologic factor
other: Right heart catheterization confirming elevated mean pulmonary arterial pressure and normal wedge pressure

distinguishingFeatures: Similar hemodynamic profile but different etiology
History or evidence of pulmonary embolism
Imaging showing organized thrombi in pulmonary arteries

redFlags: Signs of right heart failure such as peripheral edema and elevated jugular venous pressure
references: Simonneau G, et al. Haemodynamic definitions and updated clinical classification of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Respir J. 2019.
Sitbon O, et al. Pulmonary arterial hypertension related to HIV infection: clinical features and survival. AIDS. 2008.
Humbert M, et al. Pulmonary arterial hypertension in HIV infection. Eur Respir J. 2006.
